full_judgment: 2. The suit in question was decreed ex-parte and pursuant to the decree, the decree-holder-Rupali Bank, Uttara Model Town Branch put the decree in execution. The decree-holder bank obtained a certificate in respect of the mortgaged property under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat, Ain 2003 and then at its instance the mortgaged property was sold in auction. The auction purchasers who were the petitioners in the High Court Division got a sale deed registered and also got the delivery of possession of the property through the process of the Court. Thereafter, the petitioners who are the third parties filed an application under Order 21, Rules 90, 100 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain for cancellation of the sale deed and the restitution of the property sold in auction. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2006. The Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing the parties dismissed the petition on the ground that the applicants did not deposit 25% of the total amount required under section 33(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Thereafter, they renewed their prayer by depositing 25% of the total amount. The Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing the parties rejected the said application as well on the ground that it has become functus officio after disposal of the earlier application on the same point. The said applicants thereupon preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 371 of 2006 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge who by judgment and order dated 11th May, 2007 allowed the appeal upholding the order of the Artha Rin Adalat passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2006. The learned Additional District Judge however set aside the subsequent order of the Artha Rin Adalat passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 2006 and directed the Artha Rin Adalat to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 2006 in accordance with law.
